title: fix(browser): report page changes without implying revoked access
body:
Supersedes #173609, thanks @Winoren.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: browser document reads report revoked access when an allowed navigation invalidates the in-flight read, prompting agents to request permission again.

## User Impact

Interrupted reads now explain that the document changed and tell the agent to inspect the current page before retrying. Stale results remain blocked. Real revocation, restricted pages, and detached debuggers still reject commands; no permission decision changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Choose the diagnostic only after the existing access check rejects, using the existing proven-tab authority check to distinguish document lifetime from access revocation. No command scope, dispatch, or acceptance checks change.

Reimplemented on trusted main rather than executing the contributor branch. Every commit preserves human contributor credit. Simplification kept the existing owner and state: production is +7 lines because the explicit document and authority checks are necessary; no safe dead or duplicate production code was found to remove. Tests grow five lines by extending existing full-background read-completion cases to both access modes; the matching isolated allocation covers that regression. The extra relay test fixture from the initial revision was removed in favor of these existing tests.

## Evidence

- Base: `3bf7eedacd401109de8579e0a116112d489a51f8`. With the original production owner restored, the final two named test files fail in six diagnostic assertions / 68 pass, receiving revoked access instead of document changed (41.58 s Vitest duration; 43.24 s wrapper). This covers Network/Fetch response reads in both modes, same-URL reload, and ordered navigation events.
- With the fix restored: all 74 tests in `background.initial-target.test.ts` and `tab-access-events.navigation.test.ts` pass (11.56 s Vitest duration; 13.23 s wrapper). Earlier focused access-policy and command-handler tests also pass; their production inputs are unchanged. The existing background harness provides the full relay boundary; most cold-run time is transformation, and no new harness or waits were added.
- Existing revocation, restricted-page, group-change, detach, and connection controls remain intact. Chrome I/O is mocked; no Playwright, Chromium, or live Gateway run.
- Touched-file focused oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass. Type-aware lint was stopped when the wrapper entered declaration preparation; broad type/lint/test proof belongs to PR CI on this host.
- Independent Codex autoreview through P2 reviewed the complete repaired delta with full owner and consumer context. It confirmed the working-tree repair and unchanged permission decisions, and flagged one index-only issue: the repaired expectations needed staging alongside production. That finding is resolved in the published repair commit. The production security review confirms rejection happens before diagnostic selection, the original epoch remains invalid, and no access is widened. The reviewer inspected source; it did not rerun tests.
- Initial CI exposed the stale Network/Fetch assertions and an unbound-method lint failure in the redundant test fixture. The assertions are corrected and that fixture is removed. These were PR-caused failures; neither is attributed to main. Current-head PR CI supplies broad proof.
- Repaired head `f9daac241ef7b234dad63024ab1cecf91b50089e`: [browser shard passes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41332399455/job/124925496564), with 116 s total job time including setup. Production/test types and extension lint also pass in [current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41332399455).

Contributor source was read through `gh pr view/diff` only and was never checked out or run. No Team Gateway restart or configuration change is needed; users receive the diagnostic with an updated browser extension.
